title: Trial harness: enroll (randomise A/B per repo), brief, collect (session cost-state), status; docs/TRIAL.md with the pre-registered analysis
description:
The harness for the crew-vs-default-Claude trial (water-mill-166). Owner asked 2026-10-13 to build it after water-mill-hix lands, and to see it BEFORE any bead is enrolled.

Design constraints already settled (see docs/OBSERVABILITY.md trial section, water-mill-658 sluice, baseline knowledge/baselines/2026-10-13-catches-escapes/):
- ONE trial bead per top-level session. Arm A = an orchestrator session that runs millstone -> sluice -> tailrace; arm B = a solo session (one general-purpose Claude, same bead text, same "implement, test, open a PR" brief). Per-bead tokens/cost come from that session's cost-state line, read AFTER the session exits, last line (cumulative). Subagent transcripts under-count output, so never use per-agent records for the trial's cost.
- Randomise BEFORE work starts and record it in the bead (label trial:A / trial:B) and in a tracked trial ledger.

Build in water-mill:
1. `watermill trial enroll <repo> <bead-id>...` -- checks eligibility (not epic; not fence-touching unless the bead directs it; not owner-marked hand-only; registered repo), stratifies by repo, assigns A/B with a seeded, logged RNG (balanced blocks of 4 per repo), writes the label to the bead via the repo's normal bead path and a line to knowledge/trial/ledger.jsonl (bead, repo, arm, seed, enrolled_at). Refuses to re-randomise an enrolled bead.
2. `watermill trial brief <bead-id>` -- prints the exact prompt for the session: arm A (orchestrator brief naming the crew) or arm B (solo brief: implement, run the gate, open a PR, write a handoff, `agents record --role solo --arm B` at sign-off). Same bead text, same gate, same merge rule (CI green + owner/tailrace merge) for both arms. Cloud and laptop variants (cloud uses the runbook's gh api steps).
3. `watermill trial collect` -- for each enrolled bead whose session has ended: read the session's final cost-state (session id from the run records / ledger), duration, landed or not, CI green on first push, owner corrections (count of owner commits on the PR, if any), and append to knowledge/trial/results.jsonl. Escapes are scored separately, BLIND to arm, with the baseline's rubric (the scorer prompt must not see the ledger), 14 days after landing.
4. `watermill trial status` -- per arm: enrolled, in progress, landed, scored; interim look at 30 per arm; final at 60. Uses agents compare's stats (Fisher on escape rate, Mann-Whitney on time/cost), prints "too few to say" honestly, no early stopping on p-values.
Docs: docs/TRIAL.md (protocol, eligibility, randomisation, blinding, analysis plan written BEFORE data -- primary outcome: escaped bug-or-worse defects per bead within 14 days; secondary: cost_usd_est, duration, first-push CI green).
Verification: tests for eligibility, balanced randomisation per repo, no re-randomise, ledger append-only, brief text per arm, collect reading a fixture cost-state; a dry-run enrolment against real ready beads that writes nothing.
Out of scope: enrolling real beads (owner does that after review).

title: Output tokens under-counted in subagent transcripts (first streamed chunk only): measure, fix or flag before the trial
description:
Found by sluice on water-mill-cdi (2026-10-13). Subagent transcripts appear to carry only the FIRST streamed chunk's `usage.output_tokens` per message (millstone's cdi run: at most 29 per message, 193 total over a multi-minute run), so `output_tokens` -- and the output part of cost_usd_est, the most expensive token class -- is a floor, not a measurement. 441's sluice saw the same under-count in live transcripts.

Why it matters now: the crew-vs-default-Claude trial (water-mill-166) compares tokens and cost between arm A (crew = subagents) and arm B (a single Claude = a top-level session). If top-level session transcripts record output differently from subagent transcripts, the trial's token/cost comparison is BIASED by measurement, not behaviour.

Goal: establish, from real transcripts (counts only, never content), how output_tokens is recorded for (a) top-level sessions and (b) subagents -- per message, final vs partial chunks, whether a later line or a result/summary line carries the true total -- and fix sessionlog to read the true total where one exists. If no true total exists for one kind of run, say so plainly, mark output_tokens as a floor (fields_inferred or a detail flag) for that kind, and document the bias for the trial.
Also (small): `watermill agents sweep` silently ignores `--json` (a compare-only flag); make sweep reject it.
Files: watermill/sessionlog.py, tests (fixtures modelled on the real shapes), docs/OBSERVABILITY.md, cli.py for --json.
Verification: a table in the handoff -- per run kind, how many messages, sum of output_tokens as read before/after, and the evidence for which number is the true one.
Blocks: water-mill-166 (trial) on its token/cost outcome.

title: Tailrace records structured agent facts at landing ('watermill agents record')
description:
Discovered by millstone on water-mill-a7z (2026-10-13); WIDENED by the orchestrator 2026-10-13 for the crew-vs-default-Claude trial (water-mill-166) and cloud runs (cheme-cjl).

Problem: crew facts reach runs/agents.jsonl only via `watermill agents sweep`, which parses free-text handoffs and reads transcripts from the LAPTOP's ~/.claude/projects. Cloud sessions keep their transcripts inside the cloud container, so their time/tokens are invisible; and the trial's arm B (a single default Claude) leaves no handoff at all.

Goal: any agent -- crew role or a plain Claude session -- records its own run facts into the repo at sign-off, metadata only, the same way locally and in the cloud.
- New `watermill agents record`:
  - `--transcript auto|<path>`: read the running session's OWN transcript with the existing sessionlog extractor (whitelist; no message text, tool input or output -- the 61r canary tests must cover this path too). Find a reliable way for a running agent to locate its own transcript (env var such as the session id, the subagent's agent id, or newest file in the session dir) and prove it works for a top-level session AND a subagent; document the method.
  - Structured facts passed as flags: bead id, role (millstone/sluice/tailrace/solo), PR number, verdict, sluice rounds, `--arm A|B` (optional, trial label).
  - Writes ONE line to a TRACKED append-only file (e.g. knowledge/agent-runs/<project>.jsonl -- runs/ is gitignored and cannot carry facts off a cloud container), committed with the agent's other sign-off commits. Same schema as runs/agents.jsonl (agent_kind, source="recorded", detail with tokens_total etc.).
  - `agents sweep` ingests the tracked files from the factory and every registered checkout; a recorded line wins over a parsed/transcript line for the same run (no double count: key on session/agent id).
- tailrace.md in ALL FOUR identical crew copies (water-mill, watermill-cell-template, the ZIM cell, and any other registered copy): each crew role runs `agents record` for its own run before its handoff; tailrace adds the bead-level facts. Do NOT change the CI-verify rules (water-mill-1ay owns that).
Files: watermill/cli.py, agentlog.py, sessionlog.py (reuse), new recorded-source reader, tests, docs/OBSERVABILITY.md, the four crew .md copies.
Verification: gate green; four crew files diff-identical; a test that a recorded line + the same run's laptop transcript produce ONE record; a real `agents record --transcript auto` run from this session's own crew agent proves self-location (paste the metadata-only line); state plainly whether a cloud run was tested or not.
Out of scope: arm-B harness/instructions (trial bead); cost estimation (water-mill-cdi); CI-less landing (water-mill-1ay).

title: Agent log: sweep Claude Code subagent/session transcripts (metadata only) into runs/agents.jsonl
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-13, sibling of the crew sweep bead (depends on it for `watermill/agentlog.py` and the runs/agents.jsonl schema). The comparison side: every agent run that is NOT the mill crew.

Goal: `watermill agents sweep` also appends one record per Claude Code subagent run and per top-level session, from `~/.claude/projects/*/`, into runs/agents.jsonl.

Files: new `watermill/sessionlog.py`, `watermill/agentlog.py` (register the source), tests with small synthetic fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`, `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`.

Approach:
- Subagents: `<project>/<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl` + the sibling `.meta.json` (agentType, description, model, taskKind). Key `session:<session id>:<agent file stem>`. agent_kind = `mill-crew` when agentType is millstone/sluice/tailrace (these join with the crew records by bead id where the description names one: link, don't double-count), else `subagent:<agentType>`. Top-level sessions: agent_kind `session`.
- Metadata ONLY: start/end timestamps, duration, model, token usage totals from assistant message `usage` fields, tool-call count, cwd's repo name, error/interrupted flags. **Never copy message text, tool inputs or tool outputs into runs/agents.jsonl or a log line** -- the transcripts hold private conversations and runs/ is committed and shipped. A test must assert that no string field in an emitted record is longer than a title-length cap except known-safe ones.
- Outcome for non-crew work is not knowable from a transcript; record `outcome: null` and leave it. Do not infer success from the last message.
- Path to transcripts overridable (`--sessions-dir`, default ~/.claude/projects) so tests never read the real home dir.

Verification: `make` gate green; fixture tests for subagent + meta, missing meta, a mill crew subagent linking to its bead, the no-content-leak assertion, idempotence. Real `--dry-run` counts by agent_kind in the handoff.

Out of scope: Loki/Grafana; stats; any change to how the crew is dispatched; reading other tools' logs.

title: Agent log: runs/agents.jsonl + 'watermill agents sweep' backfills mill crew history from handoffs and bead JSONL
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-13: track mill crew performance against every other agent's. runs/tasks.jsonl only gets a line when `watermill run` (the headless CLI loop, cli.py) runs a task, so months of crew work dispatched from Claude Code sessions (millstone -> sluice -> tailrace via the Agent tool) left 2 outcome lines while ~78 beads landed (zimmy-life-tracker/brain/handoffs/mill/ alone). This bead recovers that history.

Goal: a new append-only `runs/agents.jsonl`, one JSON line per unit of agent work, with a stable `key` so a re-run never duplicates. This bead fills it with mill crew records; a sibling bead adds the non-mill agents to the same file.

Files: new `watermill/agentlog.py` (reader + idempotent writer), `watermill/crewlog.py` (mill handoff + bead-history parser), `watermill/cli.py` (flags only: `watermill agents sweep [--dry-run]`), tests under `tests/`, `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` (new section).

Approach:
- Sources: every registered project in projects.yaml -> `<checkout>/brain/handoffs/mill/*.md`, plus water-mill's own `HANDOFF-mill/*.md` (see water-mill-y3t; read it here, don't move it). Reuse watermill/landed.py's parsing where it fits rather than writing a second handoff parser.
- One record per bead: key `crew:<full bead id>`, agent_kind `mill-crew`, project, bead id, title, landed (bool, from the **LANDED** marker), landed_at (## Tailrace heading date), sluice rounds (count of ## Sluice sections), sluice_pushed_fixes (bool if the note says so), findings count/none-marker, PR number if present. Bead timing (created/started/closed) from that repo's `.beads/issues.jsonl`, never from the bd DB (the JSONL is what is in git).
- Cost/duration: only when the note or a tasks.jsonl line actually states them; otherwise null. Never estimate. Add `fields_inferred: []` listing anything parsed from free text, so stats can exclude it.
- `sweep` is safe to cron: reads all sources, appends only unseen keys, prints counts per project; a missing sibling checkout is reported, not an error.

Verification: `make` gate green; tests for: LANDED vs unlanded, multiple Sluice rounds, missing checkout, idempotent re-run (second sweep appends 0), bead id normalisation ('Zimmy Life Tracker-qyz' == 'zimmy-life-tracker-qyz'), null-not-guess for absent cost. Run a real `--dry-run` sweep and paste per-project counts in the handoff.

Out of scope: reading Claude Code transcripts (sibling bead); shipping to Loki or Grafana (sibling bead); any stats; editing the crew agent .md files (four copies kept identical; a follow-up bead if a write-at-landing hook is wanted); touching any other repo (READ ONLY: every sibling checkout).

title: Context graph structure: remember requires cause+tags; append-only 'annotate' lines fill structure on existing findings; review lists unstructured findings
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-05: 'the structure should be filled out.' Today 91/118 findings have no root_cause, most have no tags, none has a destination.

Scope (watermill/knowledge.py, recall.py, review.py, cli.py, tests, docs/KNOWLEDGE.md):
1. 'watermill remember' and knowledge.record refuse a finding without a root cause (tasklog.ROOT_CAUSES; 'none' is an explicit allowed answer) and without at least one tag. propose (agent, quarantined) gets the same requirement. Keep the 4096-byte line cap.
2. Append-only annotation: a new kind_of_line (e.g. 'annotation') carrying finding_id plus any of root_cause, tags (added), destination, and by/on. Never edits a line -- same rule as confirm/supersede. read()/get()/recall merge the latest annotation per field onto the finding; --cause filtering and the sweep see merged values. CLI: 'watermill annotate-finding <id> [--cause X] [--tag T ...] [--destination D]' (name it to avoid clashing with the existing task 'annotate').
3. Sweep section 'Missing structure': active findings still lacking a cause or tags after merge.
4. Tests incl. append-only (file only grows), merge precedence (latest wins per field, tags union), concurrent-writer line cap, and that recall output/budget is unchanged.
Coordinate: sibling bead adds a 'landed without a finding' section in review.py -- add yours as its own function/section. A follow-up bead will backfill the 106 old findings using this.

title: watermill review: 'landed without a finding' lag list, and --check fails on lag
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-05: the graph should never be behind. Mechanise it: a landed mill bead with no finding is lag.

Scope (watermill/review.py + a small reader module; cli.py only for flags):
- Source of 'landed': sibling checkouts' brain/handoffs/mill/*.md marked **LANDED** (registered projects in projects.yaml give the checkout paths), with the landing date from the ## Tailrace heading. Only beads landed on/after a cutoff (default 2026-10-05; findings before that were caught up by hand) count.
- A bead is covered when any active finding's refs.tasks contains its id (normalise case/spaces: 'Zimmy Life Tracker-qyz' vs 'zimmy-life-tracker-qyz') OR its handoff has a '**Findings:** none -- <reason>' line.
- New sweep section 'Landed without a finding' listing bead, project, landed date, handoff path.
- 'watermill review --check' also exits non-zero when any uncovered bead landed more than N days ago (default 2) -- this is what a hook/routine runs. A missing sibling checkout is reported, not an error.
- 'watermill review --lag' prints just that list (for hooks/tailrace).
- Tests: covered/uncovered/none-marker/cutoff/id normalisation/missing checkout. Update docs/KNOWLEDGE.md (the sweep is now six lists).
Coordinate: sibling bead adds a 'missing structure' section in review.py -- add yours as its own function/section to keep the merge trivial.

title: Cloud mode: bead close via beads-sync only; one orchestrator docs-only PR per session (no per-bead bookkeeping PR)
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-13 (on sluice's recommendation, water-mill-mb6 review): in cloud mode, tailrace no longer opens a second "bookkeeping" PR per bead.
- The bead close travels by beads-sync: tailrace exports and commits `.beads/issues.jsonl` on the session branch and pushes; beads-sync carries it to main. It never rides in a PR (a PR carrying issues.jsonl already conflicted on line order alone: f-20261013-7bbb41).
- Handoffs and run records accumulate on the session branch. The ORCHESTRATOR opens ONE docs-only PR per session (handoffs + knowledge/agent-runs records, nothing under .beads/) at session end, merges it on green with the sha guard, and then resets the session branch to main (--force-with-lease) as the runbook already says.
Files: tailrace.md cloud section (and any millstone/sluice cross-references) in ALL registered copies, byte-identical (water-mill, watermill-cell-template, zim-dashboard-demo-cell-1b, cheme-solver; Hillel via water-mill-9tx); cheme-solver/brain/runbooks/cloud-mill.md orchestrator steps (session-close docs PR).
Verification: drift check passes after all copies land; a walkthrough of a two-bead cloud session in the handoff shows no conflicts (git merge-tree against main for the docs PR).
Blocked by: water-mill-mb6 landing.

Comment each entry with why. Check the zimmy and cell contracts for the same pattern (any SessionStart hook that runs a non-fenced script) and list what you find.

title: Crew cloud mode: gh api REST, session-branch beads, committed handoffs; plus a crew-file drift check
description:
Discovered by millstone on cheme-cjl (2026-10-13). The crew agent files (millstone/sluice/tailrace .md) assume a laptop: `gh pr create/checks/merge` (GraphQL -- returns 403 in Claude Code cloud sessions), `$WM` = a sibling water-mill checkout (absent in the cloud), handoffs left uncommitted in the main checkout, and bd's Dolt database. The detailed proposal is in cheme-solver/brain/runbooks/cloud-mill.md (cheme PR #28).

Goal: a "cloud mode" in the crew files, detected by CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true:
- gh api REST instead of gh pr: POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls; GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/check-runs (poll until all completed, all success); PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge (merge_method squash); delete branch via DELETE /repos/{o}/{r}/git/refs/heads/{branch}.
- Beads: never `bd dolt push` or any refs/dolt/* push; bead changes are `.beads/issues.jsonl` commits on the session branch, carried to main by the repo's beads-sync workflow.
- Handoffs committed on the PR branch (or the session branch), never left untracked.
- $WM steps (recall/remember/agents record/review --lag): when $WM is missing, say so in the handoff and carry on; `agents record` should still work if the repo vendors it -- decide.
- Laptop behaviour unchanged.
Also add a drift check: a water-mill test or `watermill validate` step that fails when any registered repo's .claude/agents/{millstone,sluice,tailrace}.md differs from water-mill's (list: water-mill, watermill-cell-template, zim-dashboard-demo-cell-1b, cheme-solver, Hillel-Programming; plus the untracked workshop copies at ~/Documents/code/.claude/agents, which the orchestrator syncs by hand).
Files: the crew .md in every copy (one PR per repo, byte-identical), watermill validate/test for drift, docs.
Verification: md5 identical across copies; drift check fails on a deliberately altered copy; the first real cloud run (cheme-cjl) exercises cloud mode.
Blocked by: cheme-cjl landing (its runbook is the spec).

title: watermill agents report: self-contained HTML scorecard (comparisons with CIs, first-pass by week, landings, run distributions)
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-13: visualize crew vs other-agent performance with the honest statistics Grafana can't draw. A hand-built preview of the target page was published as a private artifact on 2026-10-13 ("Mill Crew Scorecard"); match its sections and rules, not necessarily its pixels.

Goal: `watermill agents report [--out PATH] [--since DATE]` writes ONE self-contained HTML file (no network: inline CSS/JS, no CDN, system font stack) from runs/agents.jsonl via the same code paths as `agents compare --json` -- the page must never compute a statistic compare doesn't.

Sections (in order):
1. Summary tiles: beads landed k of n (+ Wilson CI), first-pass approval rate (+ CI, n), crew runs by role, other-agent run counts.
2. Comparisons: for each default comparison plus crew:sluice vs crew:millstone and crew:tailrace vs crew:millstone -- one row per run metric: both groups' median dot + 95% CI bar on a shared per-row log scale; a chip with "too few to say . n a vs b" / "differs . p . n" / "no clear difference . p . n"; the median-difference bootstrap CI beneath. Session comparisons carry the not-like-for-like caveat.
3. First-pass approval by ISO week (Monday start): rate line + Wilson band + per-week n under the axis + dashed all-time line.
4. Beads landed per week, stacked by project (source=handoff only), with a legend and a table view.
5. Per-run dot strips per group (millstone, sluice, tailrace, subagent, session) for duration / tokens_total / tool_call_count, median tick, log scale; "not recorded" when a group has no values.
6. Notes: works vs runs, too-few-to-say, session caveat, what's missing (cost, session duration, cache tokens).
Rules: both light and dark themes via prefers-color-scheme; every chart has a table view; colors from a validated categorical palette; NO titles, paths, cwd, transcript names or any free text from records in the page -- numbers, group labels and project names only (test it with a canary title).
Files: new watermill/report.py, cli.py (flag), tests (structure, no-leak canary, deterministic output for a fixture), docs/OBSERVABILITY.md (section).
Verification: gate green; generated page for a fixture is byte-stable across runs; real-data page written to a scratch path and its numbers match `agents compare --json` (paste the check in the handoff).
Out of scope: publishing the page anywhere (the orchestrator does that); Grafana changes; new statistics.

title: Tailrace: explicit local-verify path for repos without CI (all four crew copies)
description:
Discovered by sluice on water-mill-m2r (2026-10-13). tailrace.md step 1 says "never merge without a green verify", but in a repo with no CI `gh pr checks` reports "no checks reported" forever. cheme-solver's own tailrace notes (e.g. cheme-solver/brain/handoffs/mill/kym.md) show 9 retries then a merge on a local `make verify` -- the crew improvised a rule break. The cheme-solver contract now has no review block (landing is supervised, local `make verify`), but the crew agent files still give tailrace no explicit path.

Goal: tailrace.md states the CI-less path explicitly: when the repo's contract declares no review block (or `gh pr checks` reports no checks configured, as opposed to pending/failing), tailrace runs the contract gate in a fresh worktree of the PR head, records the exact command and result in the handoff as the verify, and says "local verify -- no CI" in the merge report. Pending or failing checks still block.
Files: tailrace.md in ALL FOUR identical crew copies (water-mill, watermill-cell-template, the ZIM cell, and any other registered copy -- see memory: keep them identical); no code.
Verification: the four files diff-identical; a dry walk-through against cheme-solver's contract in the handoff.
Out of scope: adding CI to any repo; changing land.py.

title: Register cheme-solver with the factory (projects.yaml + vendored contract)
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-13: register cheme-solver with the factory. It is crewed already (18 mill handoffs in cheme-solver/brain/handoffs/mill/, ~77 crew transcript runs) but unregistered, so `watermill agents sweep` can't link those runs to beads and `review --lag` never checks its landings.

Goal: cheme-solver is a registered project with a vendored contract, the same way zim-dashboard-demo-cell-1b is (it has no watermill.yaml of its own).
Files: projects.yaml (one entry: name cheme-solver, path ../cheme-solver, contract), new projects/cheme-solver.yaml, docs/STATUS.md if it lists registered projects, tests only if the registry has a test that enumerates projects.

Contract:
- commands: gate `make verify` (cheme-solver's Makefile: content + lint + test), install `make install`.
- git/review/queue blocks: copy the zim-dashboard contract's shape; base_branch main, remote origin (github.com/ziggyzims1-jpg/cheme-solver).
- fence.paths: Makefile, .github/workflows/, .beads/, CLAUDE.md, brain/, deploy/ (systemd unit, Caddyfile, cloudflared config, env.example -- production deploy on the owner's Azure VM), and any licence/credential file (the Gurobi licence follows the env-only rule in water-mill docs; grep cheme-solver for licence/secret/env handling and fence what you find). Read cheme-solver/CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md for anything they say is owner-only and fence it. Explain each fence entry in a comment, as the existing contracts do.

Verification: gate green; `watermill agents sweep --dry-run` (from the main checkout, or --root) shows cheme-solver read with its handoffs and the transcript link count rising from ~78 (paste before/after counts in the handoff); `watermill review --lag` runs with cheme-solver included (report what it lists; do not fix those beads).
Out of scope: any change inside the cheme-solver repo (READ ONLY); stamping it from the cell template; fixing anything review --lag reports.

title: landed.py: recognise every **LANDED** form tailrace writes (review --lag under-reports)
description:
Discovered by millstone on water-mill-a7z (2026-10-13). watermill/landed.py matches only a bare `**LANDED**` line, but tailrace has also written `**LANDED.** ...` (and similar), so 51 of 79 zimmy-life-tracker mill notes read as unlanded although ~78 landed. `watermill review --lag` therefore misses landed beads that have no finding -- the lag check under-reports.

Goal: landed.py recognises every LANDED form tailrace has actually written, with the same rule crewlog.py uses (share one helper; don't keep two markers).
Files: watermill/landed.py, watermill/crewlog.py (switch to the shared helper), tests.
Verification: tests for `**LANDED**`, `**LANDED.** text`, and negatives ("not LANDED", "will be **LANDED** once"); a real `watermill review --lag` before/after count in the handoff -- expect the lag list to grow, and say so.
Out of scope: editing any handoff note; tailrace.md wording.

comments.author: Andrew Zimmerman
comments.text: From sluice on a7z (2026-10-13): landed.py also mis-derives the bead id from role-prefixed handoff titles ('# Handoff — Millstone, Zimmy Life Tracker-9i7.1'). crewlog.py fixed this with _known_bead (resolve against the repo's .beads/issues.jsonl); share that helper here too.

title: 'watermill agents compare': stdlib stats (Wilson, Mann-Whitney, bootstrap) for crew vs other agents
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-13: the honest comparison Grafana can't draw. Depends on the crew sweep bead and the session sweep bead (runs/agents.jsonl). Replaces what the owner used GraphPad Prism for; build from published statistics, never from Prism.

Goal: `watermill agents compare [--since DATE] [--kind A --vs B] [--json]` prints, per shared metric, each group's n, median and 95% CI, the difference with its CI, and a test p-value -- or "too few to say" when n is small.

Files: new `watermill/stats.py` (pure functions), `watermill/cli.py` (flags), tests, `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md` (how to read the output).

Approach:
- Stdlib only (requirements.txt is deliberately tiny; do not add scipy/numpy to runtime). Implement: Wilson score interval for proportions; Mann-Whitney U with normal approximation and tie correction for durations/tokens (skewed, so no t-test); seeded percentile bootstrap CI for the difference in medians; Fisher exact for 2x2 when cells are small.
- Refuse to test below a minimum n per group (default 8) and say so; never print a p-value without the n beside it. Exclude null and `fields_inferred` values per metric and report how many were excluded.
- Correctness: tests against reference values computed once with SciPy/statsmodels and hard-coded with a comment naming the call that produced them, plus textbook worked examples. Tolerance stated per test.

Verification: `make` gate green; reference-value tests pass; run on the real runs/agents.jsonl and paste the output in the handoff.

Out of scope: charts (Grafana bead); multiple-comparison correction beyond a printed warning when more than 5 metrics are tested; any ML/regression.

title: Ship runs/agents.jsonl to Loki and commit a Grafana 'agent performance' dashboard
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-13: see crew vs other agents in Grafana, which is already wired: `watermill ship` pushes runs/index.jsonl and runs/tasks.jsonl to Loki (watermill/shipper.py, docs/OBSERVABILITY.md). Depends on the crew sweep bead (runs/agents.jsonl). Owner's Loki is self-hosted (LOKI_URL on the LAN, no user/token); it was last shipped to 2026-08-27.

Goal: `watermill ship` also ships runs/agents.jsonl, and a committed Grafana dashboard draws the comparison.

Files: `watermill/shipper.py`, `runs/.shipped.json` handling (new `agents` high-water mark, old files keep working), new `docs/grafana/agent-performance.json` (importable dashboard, Loki datasource as a variable), `docs/OBSERVABILITY.md`, tests.

Approach:
- New source label `source="agent"` plus ONE more label `agent_kind`, but bucketed to a closed set (`mill-crew`, `session`, `subagent`) so cardinality stays fixed; the full kind (`subagent:builder`) stays in the line. Extend the existing label refusal test, don't loosen it.
- Line timestamp = the work's end time (landed_at / session end), not the sweep time, so history lands on the right day; keep the ascending-within-stream rule the shipper already enforces.
- Dashboard panels (LogQL, `| json | unwrap`): records per kind per week; crew landed count and sluice rounds per bead over time; median duration and token totals by kind; crew keep rate. Every panel that mixes kinds must only compare fields both kinds actually have, and the panel description says what is excluded (null/inferred fields).

Verification: `make` gate green; `watermill ship --dry-run` against a fixture agents.jsonl shows the payload; the dashboard JSON parses and every query references only labels the shipper emits (a test can check that). Note in the handoff whether a live ship was possible (Loki at 10.0.0.47:3100 did not answer from the owner's laptop on 2026-10-13).

Out of scope: statistical tests (sibling bead -- LogQL can't do them); a Prometheus/metrics endpoint; provisioning Grafana itself.

title: Owner: review and apply the human-suggested causes from PR #30 (ng1 backfill)
description:
Follow-up from https://github.com/ziggyzims1-jpg/water-mill/pull/30 (merged 2026-10-06). Human-only judgement, not crew work.

1. Read knowledge/backfill/2026-10-human-suggested.jsonl (69 suggested causes: none 46, gate-hole 16, agent-error 7), change any you disagree with, then run:
   ./bin/watermill annotate-finding --batch knowledge/backfill/2026-10-human-suggested.jsonl --json
2. Give f-20260925-fe41bc a real cause (it carries 'clock', not in ROOT_CAUSES), e.g.:
   ./bin/watermill annotate-finding f-20260925-fe41bc --cause gate-hole
3. Judge the 29 still-unsure findings listed in the PR body (16 first-pass + 13 the sluice review moved back).
4. Close water-mill-ng1 once done.

Done when: watermill review reports Missing structure at ~0.

title: Backfill cause/tags/destination on the pre-2026-10-02 findings via annotation lines (owner approves the PR)
description: Depends on the structure bead. For each active finding lacking a cause or tags, append an annotation (watermill annotate-finding) with a root cause from tasklog.ROOT_CAUSES, 1-3 tags from the existing vocabulary (reuse before inventing), and a destination only where the lesson demonstrably became a gate test, fence path or contract note (cite it in the PR). Judgement per line: 'none' is a valid cause, and an unsure cause is better left for the owner than guessed -- list those in the PR body. One PR, findings file only, with a table summarising counts by cause/tag. The owner's merge is the human judgement the doctrine requires (docs/KNOWLEDGE.md 'A machine records what happened; only a person records why').

title: Drift check must cover watermill-cell-template's crew copy (register it or a known-copies list)
description:
Found by sluice on water-mill-mb6 (2026-10-13): watermill-cell-template is not in projects.yaml, so `watermill validate`'s crew-file drift check never checks it, although it carries a crew copy every crew change must keep identical. Decide: register it (with a contract that makes sense for a template -- it has its own watermill.yaml) or add a fixed "known crew copies" list the drift check always reads. Prefer registering if `run`/`land` would not misbehave on a template; otherwise the list.
Verification: validate reports the template's crew files; a deliberately altered template copy fails validate.

title: Sync crew agent files into Hillel-Programming after 441 (stale copies)
description:
water-mill-441 (2026-10-13) changed the crew agent files (millstone/sluice/tailrace .md: `agents whoami` + `agents record` at sign-off) in water-mill, watermill-cell-template and the ZIM cell. Hillel-Programming also carries crew copies (.claude/agents) and was deliberately not touched because another session was actively working there. Its copies are now stale.
Goal: once no other session is working in Hillel-Programming, copy the three crew files byte-identical from water-mill main into Hillel-Programming via one PR; check every other repo for stray copies (`ls ~/Documents/code/*/.claude/agents`) and list them.
Verification: md5 identical across all copies; Hillel CI green.
Blocked by: water-mill-441 landing (all three PRs).

title: Head-to-head trial: mill crew vs a single default Claude on randomized real beads
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-13: "how much better is the crew than a default Claude?" Nothing measures that yet -- only crew work has outcome records, and the few non-crew runs did different tasks. Owner will run this later; DEFERRED until they start it.

Design (randomized head-to-head on real work):
- Eligible: upcoming beads of ordinary size in registered repos (exclude epics, fence-touching beads, and anything the owner marks hand-only). Stratify by repo.
- Randomize each eligible bead to arm A (millstone -> sluice -> tailrace) or arm B (one general-purpose Claude given the same bead text and the same "implement, test, open a PR" instruction; owner or tailrace merges after the same CI gate). Record the assignment in the bead (label `trial:A` / `trial:B`) BEFORE work starts.
- Outcomes per bead: escaped defects within 14 days (bug beads discovered-from it, reverts, fix commits naming it) with the catches/escapes severity rubric (blocker / bug / test-gap / quality); owner corrections; CI green on first push; wall time; tokens (tokens_total + cache) and estimated cost (water-mill-cdi).
- Size: distinguishing ~30% vs ~10% escape rate at 80% power needs ~60 beads per arm; plan an interim look at 30 per arm, no early stopping on p-values.
- Analysis: `watermill agents compare` with a new trial grouping; Fisher exact on escape rates, Mann-Whitney on time/tokens; report "too few to say" honestly.
Blind the escape scoring: the scorer sees the bead and the defect, not the arm.
Depends on: the catches/escapes baseline (run 2026-10-13) to pick the primary outcome; water-mill-cdi for cost.

comments.author: Andrew Zimmerman
comments.text: 2026-10-13 orchestrator: baseline committed at knowledge/baselines/2026-10-13-catches-escapes/ (rubric + scoring decisions in README; score trial beads the same way). Timing: crew landed ~23 beads/week (Aug 24-Oct 12, bursty 8-57); 120 beads + 14-day escape window ~= 7 weeks if every eligible bead enrols, interim at 60 beads ~= 4-5 weeks. Cloud: both arms can run as Claude Code cloud sessions (water-mill has scripts/cloud-setup.sh; cheme-cjl tracks the cheme-solver cloud mill). Blocker for measurement: agents sweep reads transcripts from the laptop's ~/.claude/projects, so cloud runs' time/tokens are invisible unless water-mill-441 (tailrace records facts at landing) or an equivalent records them in-repo for BOTH arms.

title: review --lag must not silently report every bead when findings.jsonl is missing; drop dead zim-dashboard vendored contract
description:
Discovered by sluice on water-mill-m2r (2026-10-13). `watermill review --lag` run from a root without knowledge/findings.jsonl (a scratch root, a fresh clone before the graph is pulled) silently treats every landed bead as uncovered -- millstone reported 53 lagging beads when the true answer was 0.
Goal: review --lag (and review --check) refuse with a clear message, or at minimum warn on stderr and exit non-zero for --check, when findings.jsonl is missing. Distinguish missing from empty.
Also, same sluice: projects/zim-dashboard-demo-cell-1b.yaml is dead -- that cell now carries its own watermill.yaml, which wins. Delete the vendored copy (its header says to) after confirming the cell's file loads via `watermill validate`.
Files: watermill/review.py, tests, projects/zim-dashboard-demo-cell-1b.yaml (delete), docs if they reference it.
Verification: gate green; tests for missing vs empty findings file; validate output before/after for the zim cell.

title: Estimated cost per transcript run from model + tokens (cost_usd_est), plus cache-inclusive token total
description:
Discovered by millstone on water-mill-pu9 (2026-10-13). cost_usd is null on every crew record (handoff notes never state it; subagent transcripts carry no cost-state line), so `watermill agents compare` and the Grafana cost panel can never compare cost crew vs anything.

Goal: derive an estimated cost per transcript run from its model and token counts (input, output, cache_creation, cache_read), stored as a separate field (e.g. detail.cost_usd_est) and listed in fields_inferred -- never overwrite cost_usd, which stays "stated" cost only.
Files: watermill/sessionlog.py, a small price table module with the per-model rates and the date they were taken (cite the source page in a comment), tests, docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.
Approach: unknown model -> null, not a guess. Prices change: the table carries an as-of date and the field name says "est".
Also consider in the same bead: a cache-inclusive token total (detail.tokens_total_incl_cache), since tokens_total excludes cache and may tell a different story.
Verification: gate green; tests for known model, unknown model, cache rates; real dry-run shows how many crew runs gained an estimate.
Out of scope: billing reconciliation; changing compare's exclusion rules (an inferred estimate is excluded by default there, by design).

title: Prove the agent-performance dashboard against the real Loki/Grafana; count floored lines in ship summary
description:
Discovered by sluice on water-mill-qam (2026-10-13). The agent-performance dashboard (docs/grafana/agent-performance.json) and its LogQL have never run against a real Loki/Grafana: the owner's self-hosted Loki (LOKI_URL, 10.0.0.47:3100) was unreachable from the laptop when qam was built and reviewed.

Goal: once Loki is reachable, prove it end to end, and make floored lines visible.
- Raise reject_old_samples_max_age on the owner's Loki first (docs/OBSERVABILITY.md says how) -- owner action; confirm before shipping.
- `watermill ship --dry-run`, then a real ship; import the dashboard; every panel renders data (or is empty for a documented reason, e.g. null crew cost).
- Add to the ship summary a count of lines filed at the stream's newest timestamp instead of their own ended_at (the "floored" lines from the out-of-order fix), so a backfill that floors most of its lines is noticed.
Files: watermill/shipper.py (summary count + test), docs/OBSERVABILITY.md (what was verified, date).
Verification: screenshots or panel query results pasted in the handoff; gate green.
Out of scope: provisioning Grafana or Loki themselves; new panels.

title: review: flag findings whose merged cause is outside ROOT_CAUSES (+ pending)
description: Follow-up from ng1 sluice (2026-10-05). f-20260925-fe41bc carries root_cause 'clock', which is not in tasklog.ROOT_CAUSES; 'Missing structure' treats any non-blank cause as structured, so it is invisible to the sweep, and annotate-finding doesn't validate old lines. Add an 'unknown cause' condition to Missing structure (or its own short list) so the owner annotates it with a real cause.

title: watermill remember refuses the cell template: register watermill-cell-template (or allow it as a findings cell)

title: Lag-check water-mill's own beads: register water-mill's HANDOFF-mill/ as a landed-handoff source
description: Follow-up from brx sluice (2026-10-05). watermill/landed.py reads brain/handoffs/mill/*.md of projects in projects.yaml; water-mill itself isn't registered and keeps its mill handoffs in HANDOFF-mill/, so water-mill beads (brx, 4t3, gwv, ng1...) are never lag-checked. Add water-mill's own HANDOFF-mill/ as a source (or move water-mill's convention to brain/handoffs/mill/ and document it in CLAUDE.md). Also minor: 'review --lag' returns before '--record' is handled, so passing both skips the record.
